DT-01.c01: A **double** is a tractor pulling **2** trailers; a **triple** pulls **3**. They are less steady, so drive and inspect with extra care.
[CA] **Triples are not legal in California**, but triples questions can still be on the test.
[CA] The doubles/triples endorsement is earned by **knowledge test only**; do not bring doubles to the Class A skills test.
A **converter dolly** has **1 or 2 axles** and a fifth wheel; it hooks to the first trailer's pintle hook and carries the second trailer's front.
DT-01.c02: **Steer gently** and go slowly around corners, on-ramps, off-ramps and curves.
A curve speed that is safe for a straight truck or single-trailer rig **may be too fast** for doubles or triples, because they are less stable.
DT-01.c03: In a quick lane change the rear swings harder than the front (**rearward amplification**), like the tip of a whip.
Because of **crack-the-whip**, doubles and triples are more likely to turn over than other combinations.
The **last trailer** is the one most likely to turn over; the fix is to steer gently.
DT-01.c04: More trailers mean more critical parts, so **inspect completely**; look far ahead so you can slow or change lanes gradually.
Doubles cannot be turned or stopped suddenly: leave **more following distance**, need bigger gaps, and make sure the sides are clear.
In bad weather, more length and **more dead axles** for the drive axles to pull make **skids and loss of traction** more likely.
When parking, avoid spots you **cannot pull straight through**.
DT-01.c05: Converter dollies built **on or after March 1, 1998** must have **anti-lock brakes (ABS)**.
These dollies have a **yellow** ABS lamp on the **left side**.
DT-01.c06: Put the **heavier** trailer first, right behind the tractor, and the lighter one in the rear for the safest handling.
Secure a rear trailer without spring brakes by connecting the emergency line, charging its tank, then **disconnecting** it; chock if in doubt.
Release dolly brakes by opening the dolly air tank **petcock**; the rear trailer should sit **slightly lower** than the center of the dolly's fifth wheel.
After backing under, raise the landing gear **slightly**, test the coupling, check jaws and gap, and connect chains, hoses and light cords.
Close the petcock and the **last** trailer's shut-offs, open the **first** trailer's; charge the brakes and check air comes out at the back, or the brakes won't work.
DT-01.c07: Park in a **straight line** on **firm, level ground**, set the parking brakes, and chock the rear trailer if it has no spring brakes.
Lower the rear landing gear to unload the dolly, **close** the first trailer's rear shut-offs, disconnect lines, release dolly brakes and fifth-wheel latch, pull out slowly.
To drop the dolly: lower its landing gear, disconnect chains, set its spring brakes or chock it, release the **pintle hook**, pull clear.
**Never unlock the pintle hook** while the dolly is still under the rear trailer; the tow bar may fly up and injure someone.
DT-01.c08: Couple a triple by hooking the tractor to the first trailer, then coupling the **first trailer to the second** the doubles way.
Uncouple the **third** trailer first (pull the dolly out, then unhitch it), then the rest like a double.
[CA] Operating triples is **not allowed in California**.
DT-01.c09: There are too many truck-trailer and tractor-trailer rigs to cover them all.
Learn the correct way to couple and uncouple **your** vehicle, following the **manufacturer's and/or owner's** specifications.
DT-01.c10: Use the **7-step inspection**; the extra combination checks go with **Step 5**, the walk-around.
Fifth wheel: enough grease, **no visible space** between upper and lower, locking jaws around the **shank, not the head**, of the kingpin.
A sliding fifth wheel too far **forward** can let the tractor frame hit the landing gear or the cab hit the trailer in turns; landing gear fully raised.
Shut-off valves: **OPEN** at the rear of front trailers, **CLOSED** at the rear of the last trailer; dolly air tank drain valve **CLOSED**.
Also check the pintle hook is **latched**, safety chains secured, light cords plugged in, air lines supported and any dolly spare tire secured.
DT-01.c11: Hold the rig, wait for normal pressure, **push in the red "trailer air supply" knob**, and use the trailer handbrake to air the service line.
At the **last** trailer's rear, open the emergency then service line shut-offs; you should **hear air**, then close them.
The service line check needs the **trailer handbrake or brake pedal** on; no air means check that trailer and dolly shut-offs are **OPEN**.
The trailer air supply knob should pop out at the maker's pressure, usually **20–45 psi**, when you lower tank pressure.
